operator_io_quirks: Mixed quoting in DDL: follows/tweets use backticks, user_profiles uses double quotes; writer must replay DDL verbatim.
Tiny DB (7-9 rows/table); choose_table_sizes will massively oversize vs original — no huge-table sampling needed.
follows has composite PK (f1,f2) and TWO FKs to the same parent user_profiles(uid); both child cols draw from same parent column.
Self-consistent FK graph: follows->user_profiles, tweets->user_profiles; user_profiles is level 0, no cycles.

createdate declared 'datetime' with text storage 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS'; ts_fuzzer dispatches to Date (first element not int) — but spec rule 3 says Number(scale=4) if first element parses as int, else Date; here Date.
createdate has DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP and is nullable; TS ignores defaults, inserts NULL or fuzzed value.
text is char(140) -> String(length=140); samples contain apostrophes and a Unicode right-single-quote (U+2019) — writer must parameterize, not string-format.
name/email samples contain trailing newlines ('Black Widow\n', 'susan@gmail.com\n') — literal pool will carry them; String fuzzer keeps them.
email values contain '@' and '.'; String CHARSET is a-zA-Z 0-9() space — fresh emails will look nothing like real emails.
followers has huge ints (6662425, 99999998) -> Number scale from int(11) args: scale=11, precision=11; range [-1e11,1e11].
partitionid distinct=5 but values include 23,10 — small int domain, Number fuzzer will scatter widely.
All columns null_rate 0.0 in original; NOT NULL on f1,f2,id,uid,text,uid; name/email/partitionid/followers/createdate nullable.
operator_ts_expectations: Number fuzzer on int(11)/bigint(20) columns: uniform in [-1e11,1e11] (scale=11) then +-1/+-2 perturbation; PKs become huge random ints, not 1..7.
String fuzzer on name/email/text: 20% fresh random over 'a-zA-Z 0-9()' of length up to 140/255, else original element, then 50% contaminate (suffix/prefix/drop char).
Date fuzzer on createdate: template from first parsable element ('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S'), range from min/max of 3 samples (2018-03-09..2018-03-12), fresh dates in that narrow window.
FK fill: follows.f1/f2 and tweets.uid draw with replacement from user_profiles.uid AFTER its PK dedup — so FK values are the fuzzed huge ints, not 1..7.
Composite PK (f1,f2) dedup: sample_fresh_primary_keys drops duplicate (f1,f2) pairs; with huge random ints collisions are rare, so follows keeps ~n rows.
tweets.id single-col PK -> max_l0=inf, so fresh draws never reused; id stays unique.
follows has no unique single column, so drop_unique_duplicates is a no-op there.
Likely FN driver: text/name/email fresh strings are gibberish, so queries filtering on real words ('Iron Man', 'gmail') return empty -> implausible values.

Likely FP driver: createdate range is only 3 days wide, so date-range predicates (e.g. 'createdate > 2018-03-10') get near-degenerate selectivity; ties/duplicates in small int domains (partitionid) may be missing.
followers huge ints make 'followers > 1000' trivially true for most rows — predicate selectivity collapses.
No special_cases apply (twitter_1 not in college_2/advising/imdb).
